newsitem.title: UK: Hague says windfall tax to hit UK shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Hague says windfall tax to hit UK shareholders.

text.p: Conservative opposition leader William Hague said on Wednesday that the long-awaited windfall tax announced by Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown would hurt current shareholders.

"Millions of utility shares are held by ordinary men and women with pension funds and insurance policies so anyone with a pension, anyone with an insurance policy, anyone working hard to build up a nest egg for the future will be hit by the windfall tax," Hague told parliament.

"It is a savings tax by another name. He has claimed it has already been discounted by the city. Up to a point it has but that means that the prospect of billions of pounds of extra tax has already done lasting damage to the shares in which millions of people have invested for the future," Hague said.
Hague also attacked Brown's abolition of tax credits on dividend payments to pension funds as a "smash and grab raid" on the nation's pensioners.
"This change means pension funds will be able to claim less tax back, so their revenue will be lower, their growth will be lower, pensions will be smaller and pensioners will be worse off.
"Taken together with the damage from the windfall tax, it is clear that this budget delivers a double whammy against pensions.

"The bills for the decisioons announced today will be paid by millions of hard-working people many years down the line. It is a smash and grab raid on pensions funds int his country and it is a cynical betrayal of the millions who have built up pensions and now see them devalued." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
